options: The practice of designing one database per project
The practice of tuning enterprise servers
The practice of creating a single, high-level view of data for the entire organisation
The practice of documenting ETL jobs across systems
The practice of choosing an enterprise reporting tool
questions.explanation: Enterprise Data Modelling creates a single, high-level view of data across all business areas rather than system by system or project by project.

questions.stem: What is the main goal of Enterprise Data Modelling?
options: To reduce the number of servers
To speed up a single application's queries
To provide a consistent framework for managing data across the whole enterprise
To replace all departmental systems with one system
questions.explanation: The main goal is a consistent enterprise-wide framework so departments and systems can work together and data becomes easier to integrate, compare and trust.

questions.stem: How is Enterprise Data Modelling characterised in terms of its role?
options: As a detailed design for a single application
As a strategic blueprint rather than a detailed design for one application
questions.explanation: Because it defines common entities and relationships that apply everywhere, Enterprise Data Modelling acts as a strategic blueprint rather than a detailed design for one application.

questions.stem: In the school example of Enterprise Data Modelling, what problem arises when admissions, exams and fees systems each define a student differently?
questions.explanation: If each system defines a student differently, reports will not match; defining student once at the school level fixes this.

questions.stem: In the banking example, which attributes are listed for the Loan entity?
options: Customer identifier, name, date of birth and contact information
Loan amount, term, interest rate and status
questions.explanation: A Loan may include attributes such as loan amount, term, interest rate and status; the customer attributes belong to the Customer entity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the banking systems named as sharing the enterprise definitions of Customer, Loan and Repayment?
questions.explanation: The definitions are shared across loan origination, risk management, core banking and collections; human resources is not mentioned.

questions.stem: Why does consistency matter even more when data is analysed at an enterprise level?
options: Because analytics runs on faster hardware
Because measures such as loan amount, approval rate or portfolio risk must mean the same thing in finance, risk and sales reports
Because enterprise data is always stored in a data lake
Because reports are printed on paper
questions.explanation: Enterprise KPIs are built on the same standard entities and definitions so measures mean the same across finance, risk and sales, and leaders can trust the insights.

questions.stem: Which statement about the nature of Enterprise Data Modelling is correct?
options: It is project-specific and tied to one platform
It is strategic, technology-independent and can scale across operational systems, data warehouses and data lakes
It only applies to data stored in data warehouses
It is a physical modelling technique
questions.explanation: Enterprise Data Modelling is strategic rather than project-specific, independent of technology, and scales across multiple platforms.

questions.stem: What phrase describes the value Enterprise Data Modelling adds by eliminating conflicting definitions such as differing meanings of active loan?
options: A single version of the truth
questions.explanation: Enterprise Data Modelling provides a single version of the truth by eliminating conflicting definitions of the same data.

questions.stem: Which initiatives are said to depend on the shared foundation that Enterprise Data Modelling provides?
options: Data governance, master data management and large-scale digital transformation
Website design and social media marketing
questions.explanation: The shared foundation is essential for effective data governance, master data management and large-scale digital transformation initiatives.
